observations: Photo 0: Front view of a black HP laptop with a closed screen, showing the HP logo below the screen and a full keyboard with a touchpad. The keyboard has a Windows key and standard layout. The device appears to be a small, portable model, possibly a 2-in-1 or netbook. The screen is off and dusty.
Photo 1: Back cover of the laptop, showing the HP logo embossed in the center and a power button on the left. The surface is dark gray or black with visible scratches and dust.

Photo 2: Bottom panel of the laptop, showing rubber feet, ventilation grilles, and a small white sticker with unreadable text. The panel is dusty and scratched. No model number or serial is clearly visible. The sticker is too small and blurry to read.

claims.claim: It has a ram issue so needs to be changed before it can resume fully functioning as the ram is...
claims.evidence: The seller states the RAM is faulty, but no photo shows the RAM or any diagnostic evidence. The laptop screen is off, so no boot or error message is visible. No proof of RAM issue is provided.

risks.risk: RAM is faulty or missing, preventing the laptop from booting or functioning properly.
risks.proof: A photo of the open laptop with the RAM slot exposed, showing the RAM module(s) and any error codes or diagnostic lights during boot.

risks.risk: Screen is dead or damaged, preventing display even if the laptop is functional.
risks.proof: A photo of the laptop powered on with a visible screen display, or a video showing boot-up and screen output.

risks.risk: Battery is dead or missing, making the laptop unusable without a power adapter.
risks.proof: A photo of the battery compartment or the battery itself, or a video showing the laptop running on battery power.

risks.risk: Internal damage or missing components (e.g., hard drive, motherboard) not visible in photos.
risks.proof: A photo of the internal components with the back panel removed, showing the RAM, hard drive, and motherboard.

proof_requests: Photo of the laptop powered on with screen display.
Photo of the internal components with the back panel removed, showing RAM and other parts.
Photo of the battery or battery compartment.
Video of boot-up process or diagnostic screen.
response.reason: The laptop is identified as an HP model by visible logos, but the model number is unreadable. The seller claims a RAM issue, which is unverified by photos. Multiple hidden risks (non-working screen, dead battery, internal damage) cannot be ruled out. Without proof of functionality or internal condition, a worst-case price cannot be determined. Proof of boot, screen, and internal components is needed before pricing.
